title: Don't Study Alone for Interviews
subtitle: Four free tools turn solo prep into real practice
intro: You saved a post that says interview prep feels harder until you find the right tools. What if you could rehearse the real thing for free, before it counts?
takeaway: Tech interviews reward practiced performance, so use peer, expert, and AI feedback to rehearse like it's real.

sections.heading: Analogy: like rehearsing with a band before the concert
sections.body:
Learning songs alone is not the same as playing on stage with lights on.

Interview prep is the same. A peer mock interview is a practice round with another person acting as interviewer, so you feel the pressure before the real day.

That rehearsal is why these tools exist, as you'll see next.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: interviews test how you perform under pressure
sections.body:
Knowing answers isn't enough. You need to explain them clearly and solve live.

That's why your save lists four helpers: Pramp matches you with peers for free live coding sessions, Exponent gives FAANG interview frameworks - step-by-step ways ex-FAANG interviewers evaluate you - and real questions, Google Interview Warmup gives AI speech feedback on your spoken answers, and InterviewBit gives structured coding paths.

Each one adds feedback you can't get alone. But feedback can fail too.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when practice doesn't make you better
sections.body:
If you only do easy problems on InterviewBit, or ignore the AI feedback from Warmup, you repeat mistakes.

If you treat Pramp casually or watch Exponent without practicing out loud, you won't improve under stress.

Use all four together: structure, expert patterns, live pressure, and voice coaching.

steps.narration: You start studying alone and know answers but haven't performed them.
InterviewBit gives you a structured coding path to build basics in order.
Exponent shows you FAANG frameworks so you know how interviewers score you.
Pramp pairs you with a peer for a live mock with instant feedback.
Google Warmup listens to your spoken answers and coaches your delivery.
You arrive ready to perform, not just recite.

quiz.q: What is the main job of Pramp in your saves?
options: Match you with peers for free live mock coding sessions
Give AI feedback on your voice
quiz.why: Pramp is described as practicing live interviews with real people for free with instant feedback.

quiz.q: What fails first if you only watch Exponent videos but never do live mocks?
options: You will know frameworks but freeze under live pressure and speaking
You will lose your InterviewBit account
quiz.why: Knowing frameworks without live performance practice leaves you unprepared for pressure, which is what Pramp and Warmup solve.

options: To practice common interview questions with AI speech feedback
quiz.why: Warmup is Google's free AI tool that lets you practice common interview questions and get feedback on how you speak.

extra: Exponent and InterviewBit also offer paid premium tiers beyond the free content mentioned in the save.
